spots.name: Alamo Mission
spots.summary: The Alamo is a historic Spanish mission and fortress compound founded in the 18th century by Catholic missionaries in what is now San Antonio, Texas, United States.

spots.name: Fort Sam Houston
spots.summary: Fort Sam Houston is a U.S. Army post in San Antonio, Texas. Known colloquially as "Fort Sam", it is named for the first president of the Republic of Texas, Sam Houston.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Fernando Cathedral also called the Cathedral of Our Lady of Candelaria and Guadalupe is a cathedral of the Catholic Church located in San Antonio, Texas, in the United States. It is the mother church of the Archdiocese of San Antonio and the seat of its archbishop.

spots.name: San Antonio River Walk
spots.summary: The San Antonio River Walk is a city park and special-case pedestrian street along the San Antonio River in San Antonio, Texas.

spots.name: Tower of the Americas
spots.summary: The Tower of the Americas is a 750-foot (229-meter) observation tower-restaurant located in the Hemisfair district in the southeastern portion of Downtown San Antonio, Texas, United States.

spots.name: Alamo Cenotaph
spots.summary: The Alamo Cenotaph, also known as The Spirit of Sacrifice, is a monument in San Antonio, Texas, United States, commemorating the Battle of the Alamo of the Texas Revolution, which was fought at the adjacent Alamo Mission.

spots.name: San Antonio Missions National Historical Park
spots.summary: San Antonio Missions National Historical Park is a National Historical Park and part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site preserving four of the five Spanish frontier missions in San Antonio, Texas, US. These outposts were established by Catholic religious orders to spread Christianity among the local natives.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Mission San José y San Miguel de Aguayo is an historic Catholic mission in San Antonio, Texas, United States. The mission was named in part for the Marquis de San Miguel de Aguayo, José de Azlor y Virto de Vera.

spots.name: Alamo Plaza Historic District
spots.summary: The Alamo Plaza Historic District is a historic district of downtown San Antonio in the U.S. state of Texas. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977. It includes the Alamo, which is a separately listed Registered Historic Place and a U.S. National Historic Landmark.

spots.name: Fort Sam Houston National Cemetery
spots.summary: Fort Sam Houston National Cemetery is a United States National Cemetery in San Antonio, Texas. Administered by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs, it encompasses 154.7 acres (62.6 ha), and as of 2014, had over 144,000 interments. The cemetery was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2016.

spots.name: Presidio San Antonio de Béxar
spots.summary: Presidio de Béxar was a Spanish fort built near the San Antonio River, located in what is now San Antonio, Texas, in the United States. It was designed for protection of the mission San Antonio de Valero and the Villa de Béjar.

spots.name: La Antorcha de la Amistad
spots.summary: La Antorcha de la Amistad (Spanish for "The Torch of Friendship") is a monumental abstract sculpture by Mexican sculptor Sebastián, installed in Downtown San Antonio, in the U.S. state of Texas.

spots.name: St. Joseph Catholic Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The St. Joseph Catholic Church is a Roman Catholic parish church in the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of San Antonio, located at 623 East Commerce Street in downtown San Antonio, Texas, United States. The Gothic Revival house of worship was the fourth Catholic parish in the city.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St. Joseph Catholic Church (San Antonio, Texas)

spots.name: San Antonio Zoo
spots.summary: The San Antonio Zoo is a 57-acre (23 ha) zoo located in Brackenridge Park in San Antonio, Texas, United States. It is home to over 750 species, some of which are endangered or extinct in the wild, and has an annual attendance of more than 1 million.

spots.name: Spanish Governor's Palace
spots.summary: The Spanish Governor's Palace is a historic adobe from the Spanish Texas period located in Downtown San Antonio.

spots.name: San Antonio Botanical Garden
spots.summary: The San Antonio Botanical Garden is a 41-acre (17 ha), non-profit botanical garden in San Antonio, Texas, United States, and the city's official botanical garden. The garden is situated on one of the highest points within San Antonio city limits, sitting at around 798 ft

spots.name: Frost Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Frost Tower is a 23-story skyscraper in San Antonio, Texas, USA. It was opened in 2019 at a cost of $142 million and is the first new office tower built in downtown San Antonio since 1989 when Weston Centre was built.

spots.name: San Antonio Museum of Art

hours.note: Closed Mon, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The San Antonio Museum of Art (SAMA) is an art museum in Downtown San Antonio, Texas, USA. The museum spans 5,000 years of global culture. The museum is housed in the historic former Lone Star Brewery (1886) on the Museum Reach of the San Antonio River Walk.

spots.name: Buckhorn Saloon & Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Buckhorn Saloon & Museum is a privately run museum located at 318 E. Houston Street in Downtown San Antonio, Texas, U.S. Originally privately owned by Albert Friedrich, the Buckhorn became a tourist attraction for its unique collections.

spots.name: La Villita
spots.summary: La Villita Historic Arts Village is an art community in downtown San Antonio, Texas, United States. There are art galleries, stores selling souvenirs, gifts, custom jewelry, pottery, and imported Mexican folk art, as well as several restaurants in the district.

spots.name: Institute of Texan Cultures

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Institute of Texan Cultures is a museum and library operating as a component of The University of Texas at San Antonio. The building which housed the institute is a striking example of Brutalist architecture, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2024.

spots.name: Alamodome
spots.summary: The Alamodome is a 64,000-seat domed indoor multi-purpose stadium in San Antonio, Texas. It is located on the southeastern fringe of downtown San Antonio. The facility opened on May 15, 1993, having been constructed at a cost of $186 million.

spots.name: San Antonio Japanese Tea Garden
spots.summary: The San Antonio Japanese Tea Garden, or Sunken Gardens in Brackenridge Park, San Antonio, Texas, opened in an abandoned limestone rock quarry in the early 20th century. It was known also as Chinese Tea Gardens, Chinese Tea Garden Gate, Chinese Sunken Garden Gate and is listed on the U.S.

spots.name: Milam Building
spots.summary: The Milam Building is a historic 21-story building in downtown San Antonio, Texas. Built in 1928, it was the tallest building in San Antonio and the tallest brick and reinforced concrete structure in the United States standing at 280 feet (90 m).

spots.name: Market Square
spots.summary: Market Square is a three-block outdoor plaza lined with shops, and restaurants in downtown San Antonio, Texas. Market Square is the largest Mexican market in the United States. The "El Mercado" section has 32 specialty shops and the "Farmer's Market Plaza" section has 80.

spots.name: Arneson River Theater
spots.summary: Arneson River Theater is an outdoor performance theater located on the San Antonio River Walk in the U.S. state of Texas.

spots.name: City Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: City Tower is a skyscraper in downtown San Antonio, in the U.S. state of Texas. The 22-story building previously served as the headquarters for Frost Bank from 1975 to 2019 until Frost Bank moved into the eponymously named Frost Tower.

spots.name: Acequia Madre de Valero
spots.summary: Acequia Madre de Valero is an 18th-century agricultural irrigation canal built by the Spanish and located in the Bexar County city of San Antonio in the U.S. state of Texas.

spots.name: San Antonio Municipal Auditorium
spots.summary: The San Antonio Municipal Auditorium was a building located at 100 Auditorium Circle, San Antonio, Texas. It was built as a memorial to American soldiers killed in World War I.

spots.summary: The Grand Hyatt San Antonio is a 34-story, 1,003 room hotel in Downtown San Antonio, Texas, built in 2008. It is the tallest building constructed in the city during the 2000s, the second tallest hotel in the city, and the third tallest skyscraper overall in the city.

spots.name: O. Henry House Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The O. Henry House Museum is a historic house museum located in San Antonio, Texas. It is named for the American writer, William Sydney Porter, better known by his pen name O. Henry, who lived in the house in 1885.

spots.name: Henry B. González Convention Center
spots.summary: The Henry B. González Convention Center is the City of San Antonio's convention center located in Downtown San Antonio, Texas, along the banks of the River Walk.

spots.name: Military Plaza
spots.summary: The Military Plaza in San Antonio, Texas dates back to the 18th century as a military and commercial center in San Antonio. It is the location of San Antonio City Hall and the Spanish Governor's Palace.

spots.name: Milam Park
spots.summary: Milam Park, formerly Milam Square, is an urban park located in downtown San Antonio, Texas, United States. Originally used as a burial ground, the park was established in 1884. It is named after Benjamin Milam, whose remains are interred under a monument on the west end of the park.

spots.name: Travis Park
spots.summary: Travis Park is located in San Antonio in Bexar County in the U.S. state of Texas. Once a part of the original Alamo Mission in San Antonio, the park is located across the street from the restored Saint Anthony Hotel.

spots.name: Main and Military Plazas Historic District
spots.summary: Main and Military Plazas Historic District is a historic district in San Antonio, Texas. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979, with a boundary increase in 2019.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Main and Military Plazas Historic District

spots.name: Charline McCombs Empire Theatre
spots.summary: Charline McCombs Empire Theatre is a performing arts venue in San Antonio, Texas, United States. It hosts a variety of live events — such as comedy shows, music concerts, children's theater, classic productions — and it is also open for private events. It is listed in the National Register of Historic Places.

spots.name: Casa Navarro
spots.summary: Casa Navarro is a historic site in San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas, United States.

spots.name: Norton–Polk–Mathis House
spots.summary: The Norton–Polk–Mathis House, officially known as Villa Finale Museum & Gardens, is a historic house at 401 King William St. in San Antonio, Texas, United States. The house and its collection of 12,850 objects were donated to the National Trust for Historic Preservation in 2004, which operates the property as a museum.

spots.name: Staacke Brothers Building
spots.summary: The Staacke Brothers Building is located in the Bexar County city of San Antonio in the U.S. state of Texas. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places listings in Bexar County, Texas. The structure was designated a Recorded Texas Historic Landmark in 1984.

spots.name: South Texas Building
spots.summary: The South Texas Building is a twelve-story building in San Antonio, Texas, United States. It was built in 1919 and renovated in 1982. At that time it was the tallest building in San Antonio.
